Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
3 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Deccan Herald, The Federal, Firstpost, and NDTV report five Indian nationals were rescued after a projectile struck a Kuwait-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on October 1.

02 Gulf News and Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha report UK maritime authorities flagged attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz; gCaptain reports at least six vessels have been struck since Sunday.

03 Brent stood at $102.25 as of 05:50 UTC; futures are closed and the -0.11% figure is the change in the last session before the close, not a live move.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains under sustained attack pressure, with 54 indexed events in the past 24 hours. Deccan Herald, The Federal, Firstpost, and NDTV report that five Indian nationals were rescued after a projectile struck a Kuwait-flagged tanker in the strait on October 1. Gulf News and Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha report that UK Maritime Trade Operations flagged attacks on oil tankers in the waterway. gCaptain reports at least six vessels have been struck in the strait since Sunday, a tally that includes the Kuwait Oil Tanker Company VLCC Al Funtas, struck on September 28. Splash247 reports Kuwait Oil Tanker Company suffered its second VLCC strike in four days, with a separate projectile attack at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port also briefly disrupting loading operations. On the price side, Brent stood at $102.25 as of 05:50 UTC, a change of -0.11% in the last session before the close; futures are shut. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Parstoday.ir, in a single-source report, claims several non-compliant oil tankers were targeted in the strait. As of 05:50 UTC, 119 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
